message.reasoning_content: We need to determine the crime(s) based on facts. The facts: Li XX, severe disease, wants revenge. On Sep 29, 2014, he opened gas stove, intended to cause gas explosion by dialing phone to create spark. Neighbor discovered, closed gas, no explosion. Next day, he carried a knife to a restaurant area, stabbed 20 people, was subdued. Injuries: several heavy, light, minor. So crimes: attempted arson? Actually causing gas explosion is dangerous, maybe "故意毁坏财物"? But he intended to cause explosion, which could be "放火罪" (arson) or "危害公共安全罪"? In Chinese criminal law, causing explosion by gas is "放火罪" if fire is set, but here no fire occurred. Could be "未遂放火罪" (attempted arson). Also stabbing many people is "故意伤害罪" (intentional injury). Possibly multiple victims, could be "故意伤害罪" (multiple counts). Also maybe "非法持有、使用管制刀具"? But main is intentional injury. Also "危害公共安全罪" maybe for attempted explosion. The examples: earlier similar case of fire set with gasoline was "放火". For stabbing many people, they used "故意伤害". In example with multiple crimes: "故意伤害;编造、故意传播虚假恐怖信息". So we need list of crimes separated by semicolon. Should we include "放火未遂"? The fact says he opened gas stove and intended to cause explosion, but no explosion. That is attempted arson. The crime name likely "放火罪" (arson). But if not succeeded, still "放火罪" (attempted). Usually they still label as "放火罪". So answer: [罪名]放火;故意伤害<eoa>. Ensure no spaces. Format: [罪名]放火;故意伤害<eoa>.
